questions.question_text: State Newton's Second Law of Motion, write its mathematical expression, and define the SI unit of force.
questions.model_answer: Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the rate of change of linear momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced external force and acts in the direction of the force. Mathematically, force equals mass times acceleration, F = m * a. The SI unit of force is the Newton (N), defined as the force that accelerates a 1 kilogram mass by 1 meter per second squared.

key_points.description: Rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to applied force and takes place in the direction of the force.
Mathematical expression F = m * a where F is force, m is mass, and a is acceleration.
SI unit of force is the Newton (N), defined as 1 kg * m/s^2.

questions.question_text: Draw a neat labeled diagram of a simple series electric circuit to verify Ohm's Law, and explain the role of the resistor and ammeter.
questions.model_answer: A simple series electric circuit contains a battery, a switch, a resistor, and an ammeter connected in a closed series loop. The battery provides voltage across the circuit. The resistor opposes electric current according to Ohm's Law V = I * R. The ammeter is connected in series to measure the electric current flowing through the circuit.

key_points.description: Battery provides potential difference or voltage in a closed series loop.
Resistor opposes current flow and follows Ohm's Law V = I * R.
Ammeter is connected in series to measure electric current.

questions.diagram_criteria: Must depict a closed rectangular series loop with clearly labeled Battery, Switch, Resistor (zig-zag or box), and Ammeter (circle with A), plus connecting wires and current direction.
